newsitem.title: BULGARIA: World Bank "encouraged" by Bulgaria reform stance.
newsitem.headline: World Bank "encouraged" by Bulgaria reform stance.

text.p: A World Bank official said on Monday he was "encouraged" by Bulgaria's attitude towards structural reforms despite recent criticisms by the International Monetary Fund that progress was too slow.

"We are encouraged by our talks with the prime minister as we see a serious intention to cut losses of ailing state enterprises and to speed up privatisation," state radio quoted the bank's regional representative Kenneth Lay as saying.
Earlier this month the IMF postponed a second tranche of urgently needed funding totalling $115 million due to Sofia's failure to meet structural reform targets. @
Lay, who arrived in Sofia on Monday, held talks with socialist Prime Minister Zhan Videnov and other top officials.
He said structural reforms, including the closure of scores of state-owned loss-makers and of several banks, were an essential precondition for resumed economic growth, the radio reported.
His remarks came a day after Videnov's cabinet, leading socialist deputies and regional governors held a closed-door session that is believed to have focused on stepping up privatisation.
